newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Evergreen Marine to buy eight more ships.
newsitem.headline: Evergreen Marine to buy eight more ships.

text.p: Taiwan's shipping giant Evergreen Marine said on Tuesday it has decided to buy another eight container ships at an estimated cost of US$600 million.
The company already has 26 ships on order.
"We have just decided to buy eight more 5,364 twenty-foot-equivalent (TEUs) container ships," an Evergreen Marine spokesman told Reuters.
The local Economic Daily News on Tuesday estimated the deal would cost the company some US$600 million, but the Evergreen spokesman declined to confirm the figures.
"I cannot reveal the exact figures now, but the paper report is likely an estimate based on previous market price for the ships," he said.
Evergreen will buy the eight ships from Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, the spokesman said.
The company will take delivery of 26 ships by the end of 1998, and the newly ordered eight ships by 1999, the spokesman said.
The latest order of eight vessels would increase Evergreen's fleet to 116 ships, from 82 now, he said.
Evergreen also plans to add several new routes in 1997, he said.
The firm will add Far East-South Africa and South America route in January 1997, and plans to set up South America-North America and South Africa-Europe routes in 1997, he said.
